---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 6: bootstrap estimates"
---

Step 6 of the paper simulation (ML design): bootstrap estimates and 95 % quantile intervals (QI) of
recall, precision and F1 for every dataset of step 2, as in the example Rmds. The comparison with the
truths follows in the evaluation (step 7 and `S3_Code_Simulation_Coverage.Rmd`).

**Method**

- Nonparametric bootstrap over slides: K = 10,000 draws (as in the example Rmds), each resamples
  the slides with replacement (as many as the dataset has).
- Per draw:
  - `pooled`: metrics of the summed counts;
  - `grouped`: mean of the per-slide metrics (precision of a slide without detections = 0,
    F1 = 2 TP / (P + TP + FP), paper "Case B").
- `value`: median of the bootstrap draws. `value_observed`: the metric of the original dataset.
- K = 10,000: Monte Carlo error of the tail probability of each bound about ±0.16 pp, its effect
  on the coverage negligible.

This step only adds the datasets that are not in `simulation/estimates/06_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz`
yet.

**Wilson interval** (comparison: the common interval that treats all objects as independent)

- Pooled recall ΣTP / ΣP and pooled precision ΣTP / Σ(TP + FP) of the original dataset as binomial
  proportions with the Wilson score interval (95 %); ignores the clustering of the objects in slides.
- No F1 (not a binomial proportion), no grouped estimand. No resampling: computed for all datasets
  (A-D) in seconds, without a seed.

**Seed** (offset from `01_seed_offsets.csv`)

- `seed + 2000000` per dataset.
- The mirai daemons use the L'Ecuyer-CMRG random number generator (not R's default
  Mersenne-Twister); in a normal R session, set `RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")` first.

**Run**

- Parallel with `purrr::map()` and `in_parallel()` on mirai daemons, one dataset at a time.

**Output** (`simulation/estimates/`)

- `06_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz`: `scenario`, `n_slide`, `rep`, `variant`, `model`, `model_id`,
  `estimand`, `averaging`, `name`, `interval`, `value`, `value_observed`, `.lower`, `.upper`
  (`model_id = "bootstrap"`).
- `06_wilson_estimates.csv.xz`: the same columns (`model_id = "wilson"`, `averaging = "pooled"`,
  `interval = "wilson"`, `value` = `value_observed` = observed proportion).

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# F1-score from the counts (paper eq. 3); defined if TP = 0 (paper "Case B": 0)
calc_F1_score <- function(TP, FP, P) {
  2 * TP / (P + TP + FP)
}

# Pooled and grouped bootstrap of one dataset (as in the example Rmds).
# .draw = 0 is the original dataset (observed value), .draw = 1..K the bootstrap draws.
bootstrap_metrics <- function(df_sim, K = 10000) {
  n_slide <- nrow(df_sim)
  df_draws <- bind_rows(
    df_sim |> mutate(.draw = 0L),
    # Resample the slides with replacement up to the original number of slides
    tibble(.draw = rep(seq_len(K), each = n_slide),
           slide = sample(df_sim$slide, K * n_slide, replace = TRUE)) |>
      left_join(df_sim, by = "slide")
  )

  df_metrics <- df_draws |>
    # Per-slide metrics for grouped averaging
    mutate(
      Precision_slide = pmax(0, TP / (TP + FP), na.rm = TRUE), # 0 if TP + FP = 0
      Recall_slide    = TP / P,
      F1_slide        = calc_F1_score(TP, FP, P)
    ) |>
    group_by(.draw) |>
    summarise(
      # POOLED: sum the counts first, then compute the metrics
      Precision_pooled = pmax(0, sum(TP) / sum(TP + FP), na.rm = TRUE),
      Recall_pooled    = sum(TP) / sum(P),
      F1_pooled        = calc_F1_score(sum(TP), sum(FP), sum(P)),
      # GROUPED: average the per-slide metrics (each slide same weight)
      Precision_grouped = mean(Precision_slide),
      Recall_grouped    = mean(Recall_slide),
      F1_grouped        = mean(F1_slide)
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(-.draw, names_to = c("name", "averaging"), names_sep = "_")

  df_metrics |>
    filter(.draw > 0) |>
    group_by(name, averaging) |>
    median_qi(value) |>
    mutate(interval = "qi") |>
    select(name, averaging, interval, value, .lower, .upper) |>
    left_join(df_metrics |> filter(.draw == 0) |> select(name, averaging, value_observed = value),
              by = c("name", "averaging"))
}
```

# Settings
```{r}
n_workers      <- 11
dir_estimates  <- "simulation/estimates"
file_bootstrap <- file.path(dir_estimates, "06_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz")
file_wilson    <- file.path(dir_estimates, "06_wilson_estimates.csv.xz")
```

# Load data
```{r}
df_seed_offsets <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_seed_offsets.csv")
df_counts       <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_ML_performance_observed_data.csv.xz")

offset_bootstrap <- df_seed_offsets |> filter(step == "bootstrap") |> pull(offset)

# Existing estimates; only the missing datasets are bootstrapped
df_bootstrap_existing <- if (file.exists(file_bootstrap)) read_csv(file_bootstrap) else NULL
df_done <- if (is.null(df_bootstrap_existing)) {
  df_counts |> distinct(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant) |> filter(FALSE)   # no dataset done
} else {
  df_bootstrap_existing |> distinct(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant)
}
```

# Jobs
```{r}
df_jobs <- df_counts |>
  nest(data = c(slide, P, TP, FN, FP)) |>
  mutate(seed_bootstrap = seed + offset_bootstrap) |>
  anti_join(df_done, by = c("scenario", "n_slide", "rep", "variant")) |>
  arrange(rep, scenario, n_slide, variant)

nrow(df_jobs)
```

# Bootstrap
```{r}
dir.create(dir_estimates, showWarnings = FALSE)

mirai::daemons(n_workers)
invisible(mirai::everywhere(
  {
    library(dplyr)
    library(tidyr)
    library(tidybayes)
  },
  calc_F1_score = calc_F1_score, bootstrap_metrics = bootstrap_metrics
))

t_start <- Sys.time()
df_bootstrap_new <- df_jobs |>
  split(seq_len(nrow(df_jobs))) |>
  map(in_parallel(\(job) {
    set.seed(job$seed_bootstrap)
    bootstrap_metrics(job$data[[1]]) |>
      mutate(scenario = job$scenario, n_slide = job$n_slide, rep = job$rep, variant = job$variant)
  }), .progress = TRUE) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(model = "Bootstrap", model_id = "bootstrap", estimand = "bootstrap")
mirai::daemons(0)

difftime(Sys.time(), t_start, units = "mins")

df_bootstrap_estimates <- bind_rows(df_bootstrap_existing, df_bootstrap_new) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, model, model_id, estimand, averaging, name, interval,
         value, value_observed, .lower, .upper)
write_csv(df_bootstrap_estimates, file_bootstrap)
```

# Wilson interval
Wilson score interval of a proportion x / n:
$\tilde p \pm \frac{z}{1 + z^2/n} \sqrt{\hat p (1 - \hat p) / n + z^2 / (4 n^2)}$ with the centre
$\tilde p = (\hat p + z^2 / (2n)) / (1 + z^2 / n)$, $\hat p = x / n$ and $z = 1.96$.
```{r wilson}
z <- qnorm(0.975)

df_counts |>
  group_by(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant) |>
  # n of recall and precision first (TP is overwritten by its sum afterwards)
  summarise(Recall = sum(P), Precision = sum(TP + FP), TP = sum(TP), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(Recall, Precision), names_to = "name", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(
    value  = TP / n,
    center = (value + z^2 / (2 * n)) / (1 + z^2 / n),
    half   = z / (1 + z^2 / n) * sqrt(value * (1 - value) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)),
    .lower = center - half,
    .upper = center + half,
    value_observed = value,
    model = "Wilson", model_id = "wilson", estimand = "wilson", averaging = "pooled",
    interval = "wilson"
  ) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, model, model_id, estimand, averaging, name, interval,
         value, value_observed, .lower, .upper) -> df_wilson_estimates

write_csv(df_wilson_estimates, file_wilson)
```

```{r wilson-check}
# Datasets per scenario and metric, intervals that are not defined (n = 0)
df_wilson_estimates |>
  count(scenario, name, undefined = is.na(.lower), name = "datasets")

# The observed proportions equal the observed pooled values of the bootstrap (expected: 0)
read_csv(file_bootstrap) |>
  filter(averaging == "pooled") |>
  inner_join(df_wilson_estimates, by = c("scenario", "n_slide", "rep", "variant", "name")) |>
  summarise(datasets = n(), max_abs_diff = max(abs(value_observed.x - value_observed.y)))
```

# Check
```{r}
# Number of datasets per scenario, slide count and variant
df_bootstrap_estimates |>
  distinct(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant) |>
  count(scenario, n_slide, variant, name = "datasets")

# Median of the bootstrap vs. observed value (should be close; F1)
df_bootstrap_estimates |>
  filter(name == "F1") |>
  group_by(scenario, n_slide, averaging) |>
  summarise(mean_diff = mean(value - value_observed), max_abs_diff = max(abs(value - value_observed)),
            mean_width = mean(.upper - .lower), .groups = "drop")
```
